extracted.intended_audience: Recipients of federal education funds (elementary/secondary schools, postsecondary institutions), Title IX coordinators, compliance officers, and legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted standards concern recipients' obligations under final Title IX regulations on employee training, accommodations for students with disabilities, and recordkeeping (§106.8(d)–(f)). This covers who must be trained, required training content, consultation obligations for students with disabilities, record retention and disclosure rules, and related procedural clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: All-employee training requirement (§106.8(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.8(d)(1) requires all employees to be trained on a recipient's obligation to address sex discrimination in its education program or activity, the scope of conduct that constitutes sex discrimination, and all applicable notification and information requirements under §§106.40(b)(2) and 106.44.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training must be provided to all employees (not merely made available) to ensure every employee understands their role and responsibilities when they obtain information about conduct that may reasonably constitute sex discrimination. The Department expects this training often to be incorporated into existing required trainings and does not consider collective bargaining agreements to preclude offering or enforcing required trainings. Training must satisfy §106.8(d) requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who counts as 'employees' for training purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement to train 'all employees' includes advisors, graduate students, contractors, volunteers, or third-party agents who are performing roles that are directly involved in carrying out the recipient's Title IX duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declines to mandate training for advisors, graduate students, volunteers, contractors, and third-party agents who are not employees and are not directly involved in Title IX duties, because the cost would not be justified. However, due to varied employment/associational arrangements across recipients, many such individuals may be employees for purposes of §106.8(d). Recipients may choose to train additional non-employees if it furthers compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training on definition of 'sex-based harassment' (§106.8(d)(1)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: All employees must be trained on the definition of 'sex-based harassment' as part of required employee training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This training applies only to employees (not students). The Department views training on the definition as essential for employees' ability to identify and address conduct that constitutes sex discrimination, and asserts statutory authority under Title IX to require such training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training on notification requirements for pregnancy or related conditions (§106.8(d)(1)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees must be trained regarding their obligations under §106.40(b)(2) to promptly provide a student (or person with legal authority acting for the student) the Title IX Coordinator's contact information upon being informed of the student's pregnancy or related conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The required content is modest: (1) how to promptly notify a student (or person acting for the student) that the Title IX Coordinator can take actions to prevent sex discrimination and ensure equal access, and (2) how to share the Title IX Coordinator's contact information. The Department requires training of all employees because disclosures may be made to any employee, not only traditionally student-facing staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training format flexibility (live, virtual, synchronous, asynchronous)
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations do not require trainings to be in-person or live; recipients may provide trainings online or virtually, synchronously or asynchronously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declines to mandate a specific method of delivery and provides recipients flexibility to choose how best to meet training requirements for their community. Regardless of format, trainings must meet §106.8(d) content requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training for those with authority over supportive measures (§106.8(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals who have authority to modify or terminate supportive measures under §106.44(g)(4) must receive training on specified additional topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This covers a narrow category of employees (e.g., deans or principals) who can modify or reverse decisions about providing, denying, modifying, or terminating supportive measures. Because of their decision-making role in grievance procedures, these individuals must receive the additional topic-specific training set forth in §106.8(d)(2). The Department declined requests to remove this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient discretion to educate students and parents
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations limit the mandatory training to recipient employees, but recipients are not prohibited from providing educational information to students and parents about Title IX policies and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information about Title IX policies will also be made publicly available consistent with §106.8(b). The Department acknowledges value in educating parents/students but did not extend the employee training mandate to require training of students or parents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation requirement for elementary/secondary students with disabilities (§106.8(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: When an elementary or secondary student with a disability is a complainant or respondent, the recipient must require the Title IX Coordinator to consult with one or more members, as appropriate, of the student's IEP team or Section 504 team to determine how to comply with relevant special education laws while carrying out Title IX obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.8(e) does not require consultation with the student's full IEP or Section 504 team, does not mandate particular individuals be included, and does not prescribe decisionmaking processes; the recipient determines logistics. Consultation should be sensitive, consistent with FERPA, and aimed at ensuring compliance with both Title IX and special education laws. The Title IX Coordinator's duties are delegable to a designee if assigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postsecondary students with disabilities—consultation optional (§106.8(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: For postsecondary students, consultation between the Title IX Coordinator and the institution's disability services office is permitted but not required; recipients have flexibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IDEA does not apply at the postsecondary level and students are not required to disclose disabilities. §106.8(e) preserves student autonomy and permits, but does not mandate, consultation or assignment of advisors for postsecondary students with disabilities; recipients may provide advisors or consult additional officials as appropriate and must still comply with other federal disability laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and auxiliary aids—limits of Title IX
rubrics_metrics.description: The final Title IX regulations do not impose obligations with respect to rights conferred by the IDEA, ADA, or Section 504 (such as auxiliary aids and reasonable modifications); those protections remain governed by their own statutes and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must continue to comply with IDEA, Section 504, Title II/III of the ADA and implementing regs regarding accommodations, auxiliary aids, effective communication, and reasonable modifications. Title IX does not supplant those obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping—maintain documentation of complaints and responses (§106.8(f)(1)–(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must maintain records regarding their response to complaints or other notification of sex discrimination, including the actions taken, materials used to provide training under §106.8(d), documentation of informal resolution or grievance procedures and resulting outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordkeeping is necessary to demonstrate compliance, reveal compliance practices or patterns, and allow Department investigative review. The requirement is focused on maintaining records and making training materials available for public inspection upon request; it does not authorize the Department to fine recipients for failure to maintain or share records beyond OCR enforcement authorities. FERPA and §106.44(j) govern disclosure of personally identifiable information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of recordkeeping tied to Title IX Coordinator notification
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.8(f)(2) is tied to notification to the Title IX Coordinator—records are required for complaints/notifications of which the Title IX Coordinator has notice (as contrasted with a broader actual/constructive notice standard).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined to expand the recordkeeping requirement to whenever a recipient has actual or constructive notice. Under §106.44(c), employees are required either to notify the Title IX Coordinator when they have information that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, or to provide the reporting individual the Title IX Coordinator's contact information; this helps ensure relevant information is routed to the Coordinator and thereby captured under §106.8(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention period—seven-year minimum
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department maintains that seven years is an appropriate minimum retention period for records maintained under §106.8(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may retain records longer if they choose or if other legal obligations require it. The Department declined proposals to tie retention to student enrollment periods or litigation timetables, preferring a standard fixed threshold for easier administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records on dismissed or informally resolved complaints must be retained
rubrics_metrics.description: Records documenting complaints that were dismissed or resolved through informal resolution without a finding or admission of responsibility must still be maintained under §106.8(f)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintaining such records is necessary to demonstrate compliance and to document outcomes of grievance or informal resolution processes. The Department declined to require deletion or correction of such records beyond the existing documentation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on compelled sharing of evidentiary records
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations do not require recipients to share evidentiary records to assist in subsequent lawsuits or OCR investigations beyond existing obligations under other federal regulations (e.g., 34 CFR 100.6(c) as incorporated through §106.81).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department lacks authority under Title IX to fine recipients for failure to maintain/share records outside OCR administrative enforcement and declined to add language requiring sharing of evidentiary records beyond current law. §106.44(j) and FERPA govern permitted disclosures of personally identifiable information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy and disclosure constraints (§106.44(j) / FERPA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.44(j) prohibits disclosure of personally identifiable information obtained in the course of complying with Title IX except in limited circumstances; FERPA provides students/parents rights to access education records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must follow FERPA and §106.44(j) when considering disclosure of records. §106.44(j) permits disclosures required by other federal laws/regulations or permitted under FERPA and does not authorize broad disclosure of personally identifiable information obtained during compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: No mandatory collection of demographic data without notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declined to require recipients to collect or maintain demographic data about complainants and respondents because the Department did not solicit comment on such a requirement and would specifically need to solicit public comment before imposing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While commenters suggested demographic monitoring to detect bias, the Department will not mandate demographic data collection in these final regulations without a specific public-comment process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department technical assistance and guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department will offer technical assistance and guidance, as appropriate, to support recipients and Title IX Coordinators in implementing these regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department acknowledges implementation complexity and intends to provide support to promote compliance with the final regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training materials availability (public inspection / website posting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must maintain training materials used under §106.8(d) and make them available for public inspection upon request; there is a website posting requirement addressed elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordkeeping includes retaining materials used for training and facilitating public inspection. The preamble notes that the website posting requirement for training materials is discussed in more detail elsewhere in the rulemaking.
